newsitem.title: JAPAN: Israel PM Netanyahu to visit Japan in late August.
newsitem.headline: Israel PM Netanyahu to visit Japan in late August.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will begin a four-day visit to Japan on August 24 to discuss the frozen Middle East peace process with his Japanese counterpart, Ryutaro Hashimoto, a Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Monday.
"Prime Minister Netanyahu is due to meet with the prime minister on August 25. They will discuss recent developments in the process towards reaching peace in the Middle East," the spokesman said.
The official would not confirm if the two leaders would discuss an Israeli proposal to jointly develop a new system designed to intercept ballistic missiles.
Israeli Finance Minister Yaacov Neeman will accompany Netanyahu on the Israeli leader's first official visit to Japan and the first by an Israeli premier since the late Yitzhak Rabin visited in 1994.

Japan's July 29 decision to keep its U.N. peacekeeping military units in the Golan Heights for an additional two years beyond next February is seen by analysts as a sign of Tokyo's concern over stability in the region.
Japan is heavily dependent on oil imports from the Middle East and Tokyo has blamed what it calls a U.S. bias towards Israel for the deadlock in the Middle East peace process.
A spokesman for the Israeli Embassy in Tokyo said Netanyahu would go direct to South Korea for a two-day visit after leaving Tokyo.
